gates.sentence: The period of 340.9 days is 0.5 resolution elements from the nearest calendar period (one year); that is clear of it.
The observing pattern has 26% of its power at this period; the sampling alone could produce it.

Removing any one of 8 years moves the phase by at most 0.06 cycles and the amplitude by a factor of 0.78 to 1.18; the most important year carries 43% of the evidence. The signal does not hang on one year.
The 3 bands in which the signal is visible agree in phase to within 0.12 cycles.
Searched alone, the first 70% of the time span finds the same period (332.3 days), and its periodic model predicts the remaining 133 points worse than no periodic model (log-likelihood gain -27.3).
With the time axis warped at random, the search does as well as in true time 8.5% of the time; the variation does not clearly keep time.

sentences: The best periodic model has a period of 340.9 days and covers 7.8 cycles in 428 points over 2659 days; its fundamental has an amplitude of 0.987 in the standardised units of the merged light curve (1 is the object's own scatter), and 28% of its power is in higher harmonics.
Against red noise fitted to this object, with the search over 318 trial periods included, the probability of a periodic model this good is 1 in 1,001 (0 of 1000 simulated nulls matched it).
After recalibration against the whole population searched, the probability is 1 in 1,253.
For contrast, a test that assumes white noise would have given below 1 in a billion (5.0e-20); that number is not evidence, because the noise is not white.

status: This object is not promoted: it failed window, holdout, coherence.
what_would_change_this: New data are the test. If the period is real, the periodic model fitted now will fit data taken later better than red noise alone; if it is a red-noise bump, it will not. No prediction was recorded for this object, because it was not promoted.
